top_findings.title: MCP server module fails to import under the resolved SDK (mcp 2.0.0)
top_findings.evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp/server.py:267 uses @server.list_tools(); pyproject.toml declares mcp>=1.28,<3 so a fresh install resolves 2.0.0 (confirmed latest on PyPI), which removed the low-level decorator API -> _factual.json/_runtime.json report AttributeError: 'Server' object has no attribute 'list_tools'. The decorator API IS present in the locally installed mcp 1.28.1 (lowlevel/server.py:440), so the code is not hallucinated — it is version-incompatible with 2.0.0.
top_findings.suggestion: Pin mcp>=1.28,<2 (the version whose decorator API this code targets), or register handlers via the 2.0 API (add_request_handler) so import survives on both generations.

top_findings.title: Protocol tests validate an in-test StubServer, not the real MCP SDK
top_findings.evidence: tests/test_server.py:10-74 installs a hand-rolled StubServer that re-implements the removed 1.x decorator API whenever mcp is unimportable, then asserts against it. This is why test_coverage=0.94 is green while the real server cannot start.
top_findings.suggestion: Add a test that imports the module with the real installed mcp and asserts server.run wiring, so an SDK-incompatible break fails CI instead of passing against a stub.
